definition: Raw copy of source data exactly as landed: all strings, append-only, replayable. No cleaning.
Typed, cleaned, deduplicated, conformed entities. One row per business entity or event. Engineers' source of truth.
Business-ready star schema (dimensions and facts) modeled for analytics. Stores additive facts only.
Unity Catalog object that defines governed measures and dimensions once, evaluated at query time at any grain.
A continuous spell with one team in one season. A player traded mid-season has stint 1 and stint 2.
A plate appearance that is not a walk, hit-by-pitch, sacrifice or catcher interference.
Every completed turn at bat, including walks, hit-by-pitch and sacrifices.
Batter reaches base safely on a batted ball without an error or fielder's choice.
A hit that lets the batter score without the aid of an error. Counted in hits and total bases.
Bases gained by a batter from hits: 1 per single, 2 per double, 3 per triple, 4 per home run.
Share of at bats that are hits. Always computed from summed components, never by averaging averages.
How often a batter reaches base. Walks and hit-by-pitch count; sacrifice bunts do not.
Total bases per at bat. Measures power.
On-base plus slugging. A quick all-around hitting measure.
Extra bases per at bat: slugging minus batting average.
Outs recorded divided by three. Stored as outs (ipouts) to remain additive.
Earned runs allowed per nine innings.
Walks plus hits allowed per inning pitched.
Strikeouts per nine innings pitched.
Share of decisions won by a team or pitcher.
Runs scored minus runs allowed over a period.
Expected win percentage predicted from runs scored and allowed.
Sum of player salaries for a team in a season. Available from 1985; NULL before.
Business-defined grouping of seasons by the style of play. Boundaries are set in gold.dim_season and are a convention, not a fact.
Continuous team lineage across relocations and renames (e.g. Brooklyn and Los Angeles Dodgers).
